text:
Amit Patel: Quick flag — summer 2026 capacity planning shows a big spike in hosted chat token-hours (+~60% in the high scenario). We need to decide reservation mix: how much H200 vs H100 vs additional L40S to buy/commit, and regional cushions. Lead times: vendors telling me H200 ~18-22w, L40S ~6-10w. Budget window opens in 3 weeks. Thoughts? cc @Len @Maria @Shachi @procurement-bot

Len Zhang: Do we have concrete GPU-hour numbers? I ran a projection yesterday: baseline ~120k GPU-hrs/month today, expected demand 190k-220k in peak months. If we target a 25% cushion for reliability, that's an extra ~47-55k GPU-hrs/month.

Maria Gomez: Putting numbers on the table helps. Also remember Dedicated customers are booking predictable throughput — we can offset some hosted demand with Dedicated capacity if needed. That reduces immediate reservation needs in NA.

Shachi Rao: My vote: hybrid reservations. Reserve a core of H200 (for long-context, QPS-sensitive routes) in us-west and us-east where latency matters, and top up with L40S in eu-west for batch-heavy workloads. H200 is great perf but kills us on cost if we overcommit for batch.

Todd Lewis: FYI networking/rack lead time in eu-west is the gating factor — even if L40S arrive in 8 weeks, PDUs + cross-connects add ~4 weeks. We should include infra provisioning in timeline. Also need to check power budgets for extra racks in us-east (reported one slot with single-phase limitation).

Amit Patel: Good call. Procurement timeline constraints mean if we want H200 inventory by May, order needs to go out by mid-February given 20w lead time. L40S orders could slide to March.

procurement-bot: Vendor update snapshot: 
- VendorA (H200): ETA 18-22 weeks, MOQ 8 units per region, negotiated 5% discount at 12mo commit.
- VendorB (L40S): ETA 6-10 weeks, MOQ 16 units, spot pricing available with short notice.
- VendorC (H100 refurbished): ETA 4-8 weeks, limited warranty.

Len Zhang: Quick back-of-envelope cost/perf calc I posted in #notebooks: 
```
# assumptions
base_hours = 200000  # projected monthly gpu-hrs
h200_perf = 2.5      # relative to h100
cost_h200 = 10.0     # $/gpu-hr
cost_l40s = 4.0      # $/gpu-hr
# effective tokens per dollar ~ perf / cost
```
Roughly, H200 gives ~0.25 perf/$, L40S ~0.625 perf/$ — so for batch throughput we clearly favor L40S, but H200 buys latency-sensitive headroom.

Maria Gomez: Also consider fallbacks: increase KV cache hit targets and routing policies to steer cheap capacity for non-critical workloads during peaks. That could shave needed reservations by ~10-15%.

Shachi Rao: On region mix: APAC demand is growing; lead time for H200 to APAC is even longer (~24w). For APAC we should plan L40S-first and push Hosted fallbacks to Dedicated in APAC until we can get H200 there.

Todd Lewis: One more operational callout: firmware compatibility on L40S variants — we saw one batch with a different BIOS that broke our kernel tunables. Procurement should require firmware snapshot and staging testing clause.

Amit Patel: Action items then: 
- Procurement to prepare two reservation proposals: (A) H200-heavy: reserve 24 H200s across us-west/us-east, plus 32 L40S for eu. (B) L40S-lean: reserve 64 L40S across regions + 8 H200 in us-west only. Include cost delta and lead-time risk. (owner: procurement-bot)
- Infra to validate rack/power/network windows per region and produce a 12-week readiness checklist. (owner: Todd)
- ML infra to simulate routing + cache changes to estimate reservation reduction impact (owner: Len/Shachi).

procurement-bot: Created ticket #PR-8734 with two proposal drafts and preliminary vendor quotes. Link: https://tickets.internal/pr/PR-8734

Maria Gomez: Can we get a quick sync tomorrow 09:00 PT to finalize which proposal to fund? If procurement needs the PO earlier we'll pick proposal A as conservative path. :thumbsup:

Len Zhang: +1. I'll bring the updated hour-by-hour projection and a sensitivity table (cushion % vs cost).

Shachi Rao: I'll bring regional constraints and the APAC contingency plan.

Todd Lewis: I'll surface rack/power timelines and possible temporary co-lo options.

Amit Patel: Thanks all — see you tomorrow 09:00 PT. Let's try to lock vendor calls this week so we can firm lead times. :calendar:
